incidents.vector: Attackers chained two SonicWall SMA 1000 zero-days — CVE-2026-15409 (a max-severity, unauthenticated server-side request forgery) and CVE-2026-15410 (command injection) — to gain root-level remote code execution on internet-facing appliances.
incidents.impact: Rapid7 attributed the activity to the Inc ransomware group, which stole credentials, session databases and one-time-code seeds, pivoted to domain controllers, and in at least one case deployed ransomware; CISA added both CVEs to its KEV catalog and SonicWall shipped an emergency hotfix.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion detected on July 16 across Fairlife's U.S. IT systems; the initial access vector was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Coca-Cola temporarily halted Fairlife dairy production at its U.S. plants in Michigan, New York and Arizona and disclosed the incident in an SEC filing; it said product quality and safety were unaffected and Canadian operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: Nichirei Logistics Group (KFC Japan, Kura Sushi, Aeon, TableMark affected)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Nichirei's servers, prompting the company to disconnect key systems to contain the intrusion; whether ransomware was involved has not been confirmed.
incidents.impact: Japan's largest refrigerated-logistics operator suffered a multi-day outage that disrupted frozen-food shipments, leaving KFC Japan's 1,300+ restaurants short of ingredients and causing shortages at Kura Sushi, Aeon supermarkets and other chains; some affected servers held personal data.

incidents.vector: Russian military intelligence placed fake CAPTCHA 'ClickFix' prompts on compromised websites, tricking Ukrainian users into pasting a PowerShell command that installed the GhettoVibe downloader and follow-on reconnaissance and loader malware.
incidents.impact: CERT-UA observed the technique on more than 10 compromised sites during June-July; in at least one case the group used its foothold to launch a destructive attack against a Ukrainian central executive authority. Android and Signal-based social-engineering lures also continue.

incidents.vector: Two leading members of the English-speaking Scattered Spider collective used social engineering and stolen credentials to infiltrate TfL's network in 2024.
incidents.impact: Thalha Jubair and Owen Flowers were each sentenced to five years and six months in UK prison; the 2024 breach forced password resets for 27,000 staff, took 148 systems offline and cost TfL £29M ($39M). It was the UK's largest-ever cybercrime prosecution.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure across 21 states (plus international victims)
incidents.vector: Two 'bulletproof hosting' providers, Media Land and ML.Cloud, allegedly supplied cybercriminals with infrastructure and technical support to deliver malware, ransomware, phishing and denial-of-service attacks while obscuring their activity.
incidents.impact: The DOJ unsealed a 2024 indictment charging three St. Petersburg-based Russian nationals; the services facilitated attacks causing more than $62M in losses across 21 U.S. states and several countries. A $10M State Department reward and prior U.S./U.K./Australia sanctions accompany the case.

incidents.victim: Enterprise and consumer users in the U.S. and Europe
incidents.vector: The actor tracked as UAT-11795 distributed trojanized installers for popular tools (Webex, Zoom, MobaXterm, DBeaver) via ClickFix lures, delivering a Python-based 'Starland RAT' and a bespoke in-memory PowerShell command-and-control implant.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos reported the campaign, active since June 2025, steals browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallets and deploys CastleStealer and Remcos RAT; infections concentrated in the U.S. with additional victims in Germany, Romania and Venezuela.

incidents.vector: The FulcrumSec extortion group gained access via exposed or hardcoded credentials and misconfigurations, then used AI agents to triage and analyze the stolen data to sharpen its ransom demand.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have stolen roughly 1.3TB (~700,000 files) including intellectual property for five undisclosed drug programs and private AI models, demanding $25M and publicizing the theft to pressure the company. Detailed in a GuidePoint Security report.

incidents.victim: AsyncAPI npm packages and downstream developers
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a misconfigured GitHub Actions 'pull_request_target' workflow (a pwn request) to steal the asyncapi-bot token, then rode the project's legitimate trusted-publishing pipeline to release five poisoned package versions carrying import-time malicious loaders.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Threat Intelligence found the packages delivered a 'Miasma' modular runtime with command-and-control, persistence and disabled credential-harvesting modules; because @asyncapi/specs is a transitive dependency, developer workstations, CI/CD pipelines and builds importing the versions during the ~90-minute window were exposed.

incidents.vector: A contractor published roughly 844 MB of sensitive CISA data — including AWS GovCloud administrative keys and plaintext credentials for dozens of internal systems — in a public GitHub repository that remained exposed for about six months.
incidents.impact: CISA's postmortem acknowledged it ignored nine automated GitGuardian alerts and took more than 48 hours to rotate keys after notification; no confirmed malicious exploitation, but the exposure revealed gaps in the agency's vulnerability-report intake channels. Surfaced by KrebsOnSecurity and GitGuardian.
